about: The Contrast Checker evaluates color combinations for accessibility compliance and readability. This tool ensures your color choices meet WCAG guidelines for web accessibility and inclusive design.
Essential for designers and developers who need to create accessible interfaces that work for users with visual impairments, ensuring compliance with accessibility standards and regulations.
howToUse: Check WCAG AA and AAA compliance levels
Adjust colors to improve accessibility if needed

faqs.question: What is a good contrast ratio?
faqs.answer: WCAG guidelines recommend a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for normal text (AA level) and 7:1 for enhanced accessibility (AAA level). Large text requires lower ratios.

faqs.question: Why is color contrast important?
faqs.answer: Good contrast ensures text is readable for people with visual impairments, color blindness, or when viewing in bright sunlight. It's also legally required in many jurisdictions.

faqs.question: What's the difference between AA and AAA levels?
faqs.answer: AA is the standard level for web accessibility compliance. AAA is the highest level, providing enhanced accessibility for users with more severe visual impairments.

faqs.question: How can I improve poor contrast?
faqs.answer: Make colors darker or lighter to increase the difference between foreground and background. Our tool provides suggestions for achieving better contrast ratios.
